briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Brands Push Through the Tax Squeeze While D.C. Clears a Path Forward
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding workarounds and growth even as the 24% wholesale tax bites — from a Detroit-born chain going national to a governor's-race tax-repeal pledge gaining industry backing. Nationally, a federal court just cleared the way for Schedule III to stick, psychedelics cleared another FDA hurdle, and Congress bought the hemp industry more runway.

local.text: JARS Cannabis goes national, buys into Arizona
local.text_full: JARS Cannabis goes national, buys into Arizona — the Michigan-based chain announced a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa brand dispensaries, soon making JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona.

local.text: MiCIA backs GOP nominee on tax-repeal pledge
local.text_full: MiCIA backs GOP nominee on tax-repeal pledge — the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association officially endorsed Republican gubernatorial candidate John James, citing his commitment to repealing the 24% wholesale tax.

local.text: Menominee could add four more dispensaries
local.text_full: Menominee could add four more dispensaries — a petition drive turned in enough signatures to put a cap increase from nine to 13 stores on the November ballot.

local.text: Muskegon's Fields Cannary targets fall dispensary-restaurant opening
local.text_full: Muskegon's Fields Cannary targets fall dispensary-restaurant opening — the hospitality-forward buildout pairs a retail cannabis dispensary with a full-service restaurant, pushing the format further than most Michigan shops.

local.text: Tax pain drives closures, but cost-sharing offers a workaround
local.text_full: Tax pain drives closures, but cost-sharing offers a workaround — U.P. chain Higher Love shut five of nine locations citing the 24% wholesale tax, while three-store operator Rize has sustained growth by splitting the tax burden with suppliers instead of absorbing it alone.

national.text: Federal court upholds Schedule III reclassification of medical marijuana
national.text_full: Federal court upholds Schedule III reclassification of medical marijuana — on Sept. 9, 2026, the D.C. Circuit left the rescheduling order in effect, ruling that anti-rescheduling forces had not shown grounds to overturn it.

national.text: Compass Pathways lands FDA priority voucher for psilocybin depression drug
national.text_full: Compass Pathways lands FDA priority voucher for psilocybin depression drug — the FDA granted a rolling NDA review and awarded COMP360 a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher, which shortens the standard review to roughly one to two months.

national.text: FDA builds out infrastructure for a psychedelics approval pathway
national.text_full: FDA builds out infrastructure for a psychedelics approval pathway — the agency finalized clinical trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and held a public hearing on psychedelic therapeutic use, signaling it's preparing for a live approval docket.

national.text: Congress buys hemp industry a one-month reprieve
national.text_full: Congress buys hemp industry a one-month reprieve — the House passed a funding measure 370-48 delaying federal hemp-THC restrictions from Nov. 12 to Dec. 11, giving lawmakers more time to craft regulation instead of a ban.

national.text: Brand M&A heats up as Sunderstorm scoops up Lime
national.text_full: Brand M&A heats up as Sunderstorm scoops up Lime — the KANHA edibles maker is bringing the Lime brand into its house of brands, strengthening its foothold in high-velocity retail categories as brand equity rises in the post-Schedule III market.
